summary: A parametric knowledge-integration method that augments an LLM with a billion-scale knowledge graph (claimed 1B triples) inside the model's own attention mechanism instead of an external retriever: KG2KV translates graph triples into key-value form the attention layer can consume, and HiKVP keeps time and memory sub-linear as the graph grows. All performance and scale numbers are the paper's claims, UNVERIFIED. The usable artifact today is the design pattern for the fleet's memory lane: precompute a large structured fact store into attention-consumable KV form once, serve queries with no retrieval hop, and update the store without retraining.

title_or_hook: "EAT": a G-front adjustment into odd spacing
summary: A defensive-front presentation change, specified player by player: 'EAT' is an adjustment inside a 'G' front that produces odd spacing (closed B-gaps) - the 4-down defense's version of a Tite front. The Nose moves from a 2i to a Shade, the 5-technique (Heavy) moves to a 4i, and 'walking' the Will linebacker puts him in his gap - after the adjustment every defender is standing in his final spot, so the defense presents an odd front while teaching nothing new. The stated purpose: simple for the players, complex for the offense - change the picture without changing the assignments. It is explicitly framed as the companion to 'Wick' (Will-to-C) pressures from this front family. Use as a front-identification key: when film or charting shows a 4-down front with both B-gaps closed by alignment (shade nose, 4i, walked Will), tag it EAT/Tite-family rather than a true odd front. title_or_hook: T.J. Watt's sack rate keeps outperforming his pressure rate (5th straight season)
summary: A persistence claim about sack conversion: for at least the fifth straight season, T.J. Watt's sack rate is outperforming his pressure rate - i.e., relative to the league, his rank/share in sacks exceeds his rank/share in pressures, year after year. The underlying idea: pressures are the larger-sample, more stable stat; sacks are the noisy conversion event - a player who converts at an elite rate for five consecutive years is evidence that conversion itself (finishing skill: bend, hands, closing speed, QB manipulation) is a repeatable trait for the very best, not pure variance. The post's numbers are truncated away (text cuts off at 'No one better in the sp...'); the claim as stated is UNVERIFIED, and 'outperforming' is undefined (rank gap, rate ratio, or percentile gap).
